verified: The human readings are applied exactly as decided and were not reopened: לְחֻם, לִקּוֹדָה, דֵּעָם, זֵכֶר, מִפְעַל (decisions 8–12); כֹחַ דֻּשָּׁנָה (13); the note text נ״א בְּחֹק (14).

סִיְמָה אוֹת: the primary crop s126-simah.png shows a hiriq under the samekh, a vertical two-dot sheva under the yod, a qamats under the mem, and plene אוֹת with a holam on the vav. הֱיוֹת has a hataf-segol. The current text matches.

The s124 corrected first paragraph (part_1, 'אֶת חִיל … כְּתָוֶךְ') matches the print in consonants, word division and punctuation (the ':' after מוֹקְדָה, בַּמִּשְׁפָּט and הַמַּחֲצָב; the periods elsewhere). The vowels match apart from the questions listed under unresolved. The lines run from the line after 'ע״ס א״ב.' to the last line of the page, and nothing is omitted or added.

The s126 continuation 'נֶחֱצַב … נִפְקָדָה:' matches the print in consonants and word division. The earlier substantive misreadings are all corrected in the current text: לְיָהֵב עָלָיו, מְנָתוֹ, שָׁנָה, דִּכּוּכָם יַרְחִישׁוּ, כְּהַיּוֹם, שׁוֹאֲגִים בְּלַהַק, נִפְקָדָה. The hataf vowels in נֶחֱצַב and הַמַּחֲצָב are present. The text ends at 'נִפְקָדָה:' before the Naalah stanza.

The small cue before Temukhim is ק׳. It is printed on s126, printed p.49, body line 8, immediately after 'דְּלָתוֹת לְשָׁקְדָה.' and before 'תְּמוּכִים' (s126-row3 last line and row4 line 2). It has a descender and the same shape as the ק׳ before נַעֲלָה in row5. It does not match the two-legged ח׳ before בְּשׁוֹפָר in row5. The blind reader's ח׳/ק׳ uncertainty is therefore resolved to ק׳, and the encoding ק׳=קהל (role/congregation) agrees with the print.
The ק׳ before אֶת (s124-row6, last line) is printed and encoded as a description note with abbr/expan before the part_1 milestone.

The note: the print has '(נ״א בְּחֹק)' after כְּזֶה and before יוֹם. It is encoded as a standOff commentary note with the target #et_chil_variant, and the anchor is placed before כְּזֶה, the word the variant replaces. Under JLPTEI-3 Annotations an anchor marks where a note applies and targetEnd is optional, so this is allowed. The parentheses are printed delimiters and are correctly not part of the note text.

Hebrew structure: one tei:p across the page break, with the pb at n=48 and n=49 at the correct word boundary (כְּתָוֶךְ | נֶחֱצַב). The milestones are part_1 (after the speaker), part_2 at the page break, then a bare prayer-part terminator, the ק׳ speaker, part_3, and a final terminator. This follows JLPTEI-3 rule 3 and the instruction to terminate the sequence before speaker rubrics. Each canonical URN appears once, on the existing poem div. The JSON's three paragraph:1 fragments agree with the XML.

The English text is unchanged. Part_1 matches the approved s125 review. Part_2 and part_3 match the s127 text word for word, including punctuation and '(Sarah)', as in the blind independent-126 transcription.

English alignment: part_1 ends 'Central between past and future', which matches כְּאָחוֹר וָקֶדֶם כְּתָוֶךְ. Part_2 starts 'was he hewn', which matches נֶחֱצַב, and ends 'knock at the gates,', which matches דְּלָתוֹת לְשָׁקְדָה. Part_3 'depend on the ashes … she had been considered.' matches תְּמוּכִים … נִפְקָדָה:. Both languages carry identical part_1, part_2 and part_3 URNs and end with a terminator, so the shared boundaries join exactly. The English has no speaker rubric, consistent with s127 printing none. The English is one continuous paragraph across the page break, as printed.
